questions.question: Research scenario. A coordinator sends a subagent to audit a codebase for unsafe file handling. The subagent's summary says "three risky call sites found" but gives no file paths, so the coordinator cannot write the fix tickets. What is the best change? The requirement is a repeatable handoff for future audits, rather than one-time recovery of this run.

options.A: In the task description, require a fixed return format that lists each finding with its file path and line, plus an obstacles section.
options.B: Pass the coordinator's whole conversation history to the subagent so that it understands why the paths matter.
options.C: Have the coordinator open the subagent's transcript afterwards and pull the paths out of its tool calls.
options.D: Drop the subagent and let the coordinator run the whole audit itself so that nothing is lost in a summary.

questions.rationale: Objective 1.3. A bounded return contract supplies the locators and unresolved obstacles the coordinator needs. B adds history without requiring the missing outputs. C can be useful recovery because current Claude Code persists subagent transcripts, but reading a transcript after every run does not repair the stated repeatable handoff. D removes the chosen isolation without fixing the contract. A is the best fit for this requirement; transcript persistence is not automatic inclusion in the parent context.

questions.question: Code generation scenario. A team builds an Agent SDK app that must reject a Write call when its proposed config-file content contains a known secret marker. They register a PostToolUse callback on Write that scans the new file and returns extra context telling Claude a key was found. In testing, a key still lands on disk. Which change prevents that matched Write call? Assume this callback receives the complete proposed content and reliably detects the marker.

options.A: The callback must exit with code 2 instead of returning an object, because exit 2 is how SDK hooks block.
options.B: The write has already run when PostToolUse fires; move the check to a PreToolUse callback that returns a deny permission decision with a reason.
options.C: The callback needs a stronger message in its context, so that Claude undoes the write itself every time.
options.D: Add "never write secrets" to CLAUDE.md, so Claude avoids the write and the hook only catches rare misses.

questions.rationale: Objective 1.5. PostToolUse runs after Write, so it cannot prevent that original write; context/output changes do not undo its disk effect. Prevention has to happen before the call: a PreToolUse callback blocks by returning `permissionDecision: "deny"` inside `hookSpecificOutput`, plus a reason. A mixes up SDK callbacks with Claude Code shell hooks; SDK callbacks use no exit codes. C hopes the model fixes it, which is a request, not a guarantee. D is also a request. This blocks the matched call under the stated detector contract; it does not prove every secret or alternative write path is covered. Enforce broader policy at every effect boundary and test failure handling.
questions.source: Project-authored. https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/hooks (checked 2026-10-21; rewritten as an SDK case in PLAN-02 fix round 1, via 13-Plans/active/PLAN-02-evidence/phase3-research.md X1, X2). Objective 1.5. Change-list row P8.

questions.question: Support tooling scenario. Your MCP server offers three things: a read-only list of ticket queues that the app shows when a user types @, a "summarise this ticket" template that users start from a slash command, and a create_ticket action. Which mapping of MCP primitives is right?

options.A: All three are tools, because Claude needs to be able to reach each of them during a conversation.
options.B: The queue list is a resource the app controls, the template is a prompt the user starts, and create_ticket is a tool the model calls.
options.C: The queue list is a tool, the template is a resource, and create_ticket is a prompt, since prompts can carry out actions.
options.D: The queue list and create_ticket are resources, because resources can both read and write data, and the template is a tool.

questions.rationale: Objective 2.4. The three primitives differ by who is in control: tools are model-controlled, resources are app-controlled (fetched for UI or added context, not for actions), and prompts are user-controlled (a click or slash command). A makes everything a tool and loses the app and user entry points. C and D swap the roles; resources are for reading, not acting. These are protocol interaction conventions; a host still mediates access. Tools can perform read queries as well as writes, so read-only content alone does not decide the primitive.

questions.question: Developer productivity scenario. A team connects many MCP servers to Claude Code and worries that tool definitions will fill the context window before work starts. One server is used on nearly every turn. What should they do?

options.A: Cut the setup down to a small fixed number of servers so that the definitions fit in context.
options.B: Keep tool search, which is on by default and defers tool definitions until needed, and mark only the every-turn server to always load.
options.C: Set ENABLE_TOOL_SEARCH=false so that every definition is loaded once at the start and never fetched again.
options.D: Move to a model with a larger context window so that all the definitions fit at once.

questions.rationale: Objective 2.4. In current Claude Code, tool search is on by default: MCP tool definitions are deferred and found on demand, and a server that is needed every turn can be exempted by setting `alwaysLoad: true` in its MCP configuration ("Exempt a server from deferral"). The 10% figure in some course material belongs to the opt-in ENABLE_TOOL_SEARCH=auto threshold mode, not the default. A removes useful servers to solve a problem the default already handles. C turns tool search off, which loads everything up front. D postpones the problem instead of fixing it.
questions.source: Project-authored. https://code.claude.com/docs/en/mcp, sections "Configure tool search" and "Exempt a server from deferral" (checked 2026-10-21). Objective 2.4. Change-list row P7.

questions.question: Batch processing scenario. An architect sends a nightly Message Batches job. Each request can use the web search server tool and an in-house lookup_order client tool. Assume this server-tool execution completes without a pause_turn or mixed parallel client-tool dependency. Which capability can be executed by Anthropic without a client-tool follow-up?

options.A: Both, because every tool declared in the request is run for you inside the batch.
options.B: Neither, because tools cannot be used in batch requests at all.
options.C: Web search is server-executed; lookup_order requires an external runtime to execute it and return a tool_result.
options.D: Only lookup_order, as long as tool_choice forces it, because forcing a tool makes the platform run it.

questions.rationale: Objective 4.5, supplementary tool-execution boundary in a batch workflow. Under the stated completion assumptions C is correct. A confuses declaration with execution. B incorrectly rules out supported server tools. D confuses forced selection with actual tool execution. Server tools may otherwise pause and need continuation; a client-tool runtime can be implemented by your code or supplied by a supported SDK/host. This does not claim that every server tool or feature combination is supported in Message Batches.

questions.question: API agent scenario. A long-running research agent built on the Messages API is getting slow and expensive. Its history is full of large, stale tool results it no longer needs, and it must keep its earlier decisions. Its system prompt and tool list never change, caching is supported for the chosen model, and a durable decisions record is preserved separately. Which two changes fit these needs?

options.A: Turn on context editing to clear old tool results, which are replaced with a placeholder before the prompt reaches Claude.
options.B: Turn on prompt caching for the stable prefix, expecting it to free up room in the context window.
options.C: Use prompt caching on the unchanging system prompt and tools to cut the cost of resending them.
options.D: Compact the history and trust the summary to keep every detail, so no facts need to be saved elsewhere.

questions.rationale: Objective 5.1. Each need has its own lever. Context editing clears old tool results server-side (oldest first, with a placeholder) while your client keeps the full history. Prompt caching cuts the cost and latency of a stable prefix, but it does not shrink the context. B is the trap: caching frees no space. D is the other trap: compaction can drop detail, so decisions that must survive belong in a preserved-facts block or file. The docs say server-side compaction is generally preferred for long conversations, so it is a fair add-on once the key facts are saved. Preserve the decisions record before clearing evidence. Editing earlier content can invalidate part of a cached prefix: measure the net token and latency effect rather than assume the two savings simply add. Prompt caching is not a guarantee of cache hits.

questions.question:
The user requests proposed notes in the reply only. Which invocation best satisfies that request while minimizing capabilities? The specialist must inspect the source contract rather than rely on the parent summary.

Initial situation

Prepare vendor contract review notes. Application-owned pseudocode: delegate(job="inventory clauses", source="vendor-contract.txt", output="clause-notes.txt"). Fictional company policy: classify clauses for human review; do not provide legal advice. This is a fresh, non-forked SDK subagent. The parent read the contract but has not copied its text into the invocation. Both files already exist. The host restricts file access to these two files.

options.A: Pass source path and parent summary; grant no tools and return proposed notes.
options.B: Pass source path and review boundary; grant Read and Edit for the notes file.
options.C: Pass source path and review boundary; grant Read and return proposed notes.
options.D: Pass source path and review boundary; grant Edit and return proposed notes.

questions.rationale: A fresh subagent needs an explicit task and source path. Source inspection requires Read; returning proposed notes requires no editing capability. The host file boundary remains necessary.

explain.A: A summary-only review can work for a summary task, but this task explicitly requires inspecting the source contract.
explain.B: The file boundary is narrow, but Edit is unnecessary for the reply-only request and exceeds its output authorization.
explain.C: Fits source inspection and reply-only delivery with the minimum required tool capability.
explain.D: An edit tool can support a later annotation task, but it does not supply the required source-reading capability here.

why_not.A: A summary-only review can work for a summary task, but this task explicitly requires inspecting the source contract.
why_not.B: The file boundary is narrow, but Edit is unnecessary for the reply-only request and exceeds its output authorization.
why_not.D: An edit tool can support a later annotation task, but it does not supply the required source-reading capability here.

questions.question:
What should this gate do for this payment attempt?

Initial situation

Gate a treasury payment batch. Application-owned pseudocode: send_payment(batch_digest="payroll-october") passes through a PreToolUse gate. A trusted approval store binds an approver decision to that exact digest. This is a fictional treasury policy. The gate is on the only execution route; other permission checks already permit this batch. Approval lookup returns MISSING.

options.A: Deny payment and hand off the batch digest plus the missing approval requirement.
options.B: Ask for approval in the conversation, then allow on an affirmative user reply.
options.C: Run payment, then hold the completion message until the approval lookup succeeds.
options.D: Allow the batch because the general tool permission check already passed.

questions.rationale: The required trusted evidence is missing. A pre-execution denial enforces the prerequisite; an attributable handoff enables resolution without asserting payment happened.

explain.A: This enforces the missing prerequisite and provides a concrete resolution path.
explain.B: Conversational approval may support a workflow, but this stated policy requires a trusted digest-bound store record before execution.
explain.C: Withholding a message can gate communication but cannot prevent an unapproved payment effect.
explain.D: Tool permission authorizes a capability; it does not establish this batch-specific business prerequisite.

why_not.B: Conversational approval may support a workflow, but this stated policy requires a trusted digest-bound store record before execution.
why_not.C: Withholding a message can gate communication but cannot prevent an unapproved payment effect.
why_not.D: Tool permission authorizes a capability; it does not establish this batch-specific business prerequisite.

questions.question:
Which server response best preserves the failure type and enables a useful next step?

Initial situation

Recover a campaign forecast request. Application-owned tool and business rule: forecast_campaign requires start_date to fall inside the open planning period. MCP tools/call is well formed and the tool name is registered. Execution rejects start_date because it is in a closed period. Custom recovery code CLOSED_PERIOD is application-owned, not an MCP standard code.

options.A: Return isError:false with a structured rejected status and an empty forecast.
options.B: Return a JSON-RPC invalid-params error with the accepted date range attached.
options.C: Return isError:true with an actionable date explanation and custom error category.
options.D: Return isError:true with a transient-failure category and retry the same date.

questions.rationale: The request reached a known tool; business validation failed. An error tool result can explain the accepted planning period so the caller can obtain or provide a valid date. Custom codes must be documented as application data.

explain.A: A structured business outcome can be intentional in another contract, but this rejected tool execution should be surfaced as an error here.
explain.B: Actionable detail is useful, but this well-formed call failed the tool business rule rather than the protocol request schema.
explain.C: The known tool ran and rejected a business input, so the tool-result error channel fits.
explain.D: The error channel is correct, but the category and unchanged retry do not fit a deterministic closed-period rule.

why_not.A: A structured business outcome can be intentional in another contract, but this rejected tool execution should be surfaced as an error here.
why_not.B: Actionable detail is useful, but this well-formed call failed the tool business rule rather than the protocol request schema.
why_not.D: The error channel is correct, but the category and unchanged retry do not fit a deterministic closed-period rule.

questions.question:
Which response and recovery now fit this forecast attempt?

Only failure layer changes: discovery is stale and the server now rejects the tool name as unknown before execution.

Recover a campaign forecast request. Application-owned tool and business rule: forecast_campaign requires start_date to fall inside the open planning period. MCP tools/call is well formed, but the server rejects the tool name as unknown before any execution; the supplied date remains in the closed planning period but business validation has not run. Custom recovery code CLOSED_PERIOD is application-owned, not an MCP standard code.

options.A: Return an invalid-params protocol error and request the current tool schema.
options.B: Return a transient tool error and retry the same name after a short backoff.
options.C: Return isError:true with the closed-period category and request a different date.
options.D: Return an unknown-tool protocol error and refresh discovery before another call.

questions.rationale: An unknown tool is a protocol-level issue in the cited MCP specification. Reconcile the server tool list and schema before issuing a new call; do not infer business validation that never ran.

explain.A: Refreshing the schema can help, but the observed failure is unknown dispatch, not a malformed call or parameter structure.
explain.B: Backoff is useful for temporary service faults, but the observed unknown name requires discovery rather than an assumed retryable execution fault.
explain.C: The date is still unsuitable, but no tool executed; reporting that as the observed failure misidentifies this attempt.
explain.D: Repair the unresolved tool name before addressing any subsequent business validation.

why_not.A: Refreshing the schema can help, but the observed failure is unknown dispatch, not a malformed call or parameter structure.
why_not.B: Backoff is useful for temporary service faults, but the observed unknown name requires discovery rather than an assumed retryable execution fault.
why_not.C: The date is still unsuitable, but no tool executed; reporting that as the observed failure misidentifies this attempt.

Keeping .mcp.json as the configuration source, which sequence fixes the missing evidence?

Initial situation

Read the current campaign brief. Genuine SDK option fragment: settingSources: ["user"]. A reviewed project-root .mcp.json defines the fictional campaign-library server and its read_campaign_brief tool. Authentication and server permissions are valid. Application diagnostic: project configuration was not loaded; campaign-library is absent. The prompt requests facts from the current campaign brief, which is not in the conversation.

options.A: Include project settings, verify tool discovery, and then read the requested brief.
options.B: Keep settings unchanged; copy the reviewed server definition into mcpServers in code.
options.C: Keep settings unchanged; add only a permission rule for the library reader.
options.D: Keep settings unchanged; invoke the library reader by its fully qualified tool name.

explain.A: Loads the chosen project configuration source and retrieves the missing campaign evidence.
explain.B: Direct configuration can connect a server, but violates the question requirement to retain .mcp.json as the configuration source.
explain.C: This would address denied access to an already configured tool, but the diagnostic identifies a missing server definition.
explain.D: A fully qualified name selects an available tool, but cannot instantiate the excluded project server configuration.

why_not.B: Direct configuration can connect a server, but violates the question requirement to retain .mcp.json as the configuration source.
why_not.C: This would address denied access to an already configured tool, but the diagnostic identifies a missing server definition.
why_not.D: A fully qualified name selects an available tool, but cannot instantiate the excluded project server configuration.

Initial situation

Attach a CI review to the right candidate. Job: check one automated review before a finance software merge. A digest is an application identifier for the exact source snapshot and all review inputs. Application-owned CI pseudocode, not Claude API fields:
review_input_digest = "diff-violet-7"
current_candidate_digest = "diff-violet-7"
process_exit = 0
artifacts_verified = true
CLI JSON excerpt using documented field: {"structured_output":{"findings":[]}}
The findings schema and digest format are application-owned. All authentication, parsing, schema, and required deterministic test checks have passed. The digest includes the exact source snapshot and review inputs. The gate requires a verified automated review of the candidate, with retained input and result evidence. Every source change is in review scope; there is no carry-forward exemption.

options.A: Pass from process_exit alone and discard the parsed result artifact.
options.B: Pass this review gate and retain the candidate-bound artifact.
options.C: Hold until the findings array includes one completion record for each input file.
options.D: Hold and rerun without structured output to corroborate the empty findings.

explain.A: Process success alone would not establish schema validity or candidate binding, and discarding result evidence conflicts with the retained-audit requirement.
explain.B: The valid review matches the current candidate; the stipulated acceptance conditions are satisfied.
explain.C: This schema contains actual findings, not per-file completion records. The premise already verifies the artifact and its review inputs; a valid empty findings list is not itself an incomplete review.
explain.D: Corroboration can be useful when evidence is uncertain, but the stated completion, parsing, schema, candidate binding and deterministic checks are already verified; this gate has no unresolved condition requiring another generation.

questions.question:
A fictional lending team's coordinator invoked three specialist tools in one Claude turn. The arrears query timed out before returning data; the other specialists succeeded. There is time for the permitted retry. Which handling best follows the protocol and the recovery contract?

Initial situation

Recover a missing loan review specialist result. Application-owned pseudocode, not SDK fields: loan_review={income_specialist:complete, collateral_specialist:complete, arrears_specialist:{state:failed, cause:read_timeout, attempts:1}}. Fictional recovery table: read_timeout -> exactly one further retry when time remains, then refer unresolved failure to its owner; access_denied -> refer to access owner, never retry under the same credentials. All specialists are read-only and share a still-valid snapshot. Publication requires all three results.

options.A: Return all three outcomes, retain successes, and retry only the timed-out read once.
options.B: Return all results with the arrears error marked, retain successes, and immediately request access-owner intervention.
options.C: Return the two successes now; return the arrears tool result only after recovery.
options.D: Restart all three read-only checks under the same snapshot and retain the prior results for audit.

questions.rationale: Account for every requested tool call, including the failed call. Preserve the two successful specialist results and follow the stated mandatory timeout-retry rule. If that retry fails, retain the failure and refer it; never treat an attempted retry as completed evidence.

explain.A: Each requested call receives a correlated outcome, including the error. The fictional policy requires the one remaining retry while time permits; successful results are retained. Publish only if the required check subsequently succeeds.
explain.B: The stated failure is a transient timeout with a remaining permitted retry, not an access denial.
explain.C: This leaves one call from the same assistant turn unanswered in the next user message.
explain.D: Rechecking successful specialists is unnecessary under the still-valid snapshot and does not follow the cause-specific recovery rule for the blocked specialist.

why_not.B: The stated failure is a transient timeout with a remaining permitted retry, not an access denial.
why_not.C: This leaves one call from the same assistant turn unanswered in the next user message.
why_not.D: Rechecking successful specialists is unnecessary under the still-valid snapshot and does not follow the cause-specific recovery rule for the blocked specialist.

A marketing assistant prepares an internal copy brief for counsel review. The fictional team's rule allows it to select one conflicting claim only when the supplied evidence establishes precedence; otherwise it must flag the conflict. What should the brief say?

Initial situation

Resolve conflicting approved advertising claims. Application-owned document inventory, not API configuration: Campaign Claims Pack, signed September 10: 'For the Northstar campaign, approved copy is up to 20% less setup time.' Counsel Review Bulletin, signed September 12: 'For the Northstar campaign, approved copy is up to 30% less setup time.' Both refer to the same product, audience and test population. options.B: Choose 30% provisionally, cite the bulletin and footnote that precedence remains unresolved.
options.C: Report both claims with source citations and request a precedence decision before choosing copy.

explain.B: The policy requires established precedence before choosing one conflicting claim. A disclaimer does not supply that missing decision authority.
explain.C: The evidence supports each assertion and their conflict, but does not establish which governs this campaign.
explain.D: Numerical conservatism does not establish the supplied team's approval status or resolve the documentary conflict.

why_not.B: The policy requires established precedence before choosing one conflicting claim. A disclaimer does not supply that missing decision authority.
